lede: Down-regulation ran to 6,480 MWh and cost 9.7 million TL. Almost all of it landed between 03:00 and 12:00, the hours solar was strongest.

figures.n: TL/MWh, 9% below the same weekday a week earlier
TL/MWh, 28% wider than a week earlier
TL, of which 9.7M was turning generation down

mixNote: Renewables took 55.4% of the day, five points more than the same weekday a week earlier. Wind rose 41% week on week and gas fell 30%.
solarNote: Solar supplied 183,515 MWh. Of that, 145,787 MWh came from distributed rooftop capacity that files no schedule and appears in the data only as consumption that never showed up.
tableNote: The three hours where up-regulation cost the most, with the raw wedge and the same wedge after re-clearing the day-ahead supply curve with the extra demand.
closing: All three hours deviated in the same direction on at least three of the last four same weekdays, so none of them was a surprise. Of the day's instructions, 1,500 MWh carried a grid-constraint code rather than a market imbalance code, so part of this was the network rather than the schedule.
